1|# FreeCAD gap test: is there a "teacher can, student can't" gap on a harder, less common tool? (DRAFT)
2|
3|Status: DRAFT by Claude, 2026-10-29, from the user's idea (the product is the factory; show it on a tool where Glimmer is
4|weak) and the other Claude pane's validation advice (hivey m1793292625890-145). Needs: the user's yes + budget answer,
5|free checks, verifier check, then Muse Code (runner adapter + sandbox) and the paid run. Time box: ≤ 3 h, ≤ $3.50.
6|
7|## Question
8|On the same 30 held-out jobs, written as neutral text, does Glimmer + a FreeCAD manual fail much more often than
9|Spark Open + the same manual? If so, FreeCAD is the factory's training target (a bigger, more visible gain).
10|
11|## Design (decisions)
12|- Same 30 job texts (experiments/first-test/jobs.py), scanned for CadQuery words (Workplane, ">Z" selectors, box()
13|  centring hints) and made neutral before freezing. Why: CadQuery words would push the model toward CadQuery.
14|- Same references and referee: answers are FreeCAD Python that must export the part to a fixed STEP path; the runner
15|  reads ONLY that path and scores it with experiments/first-test/checks.py at 0.2% (same yardstick as the baseline),
16|  1e-6 also reported. Why: no new exam = no new exam bugs.
17|- FreeCAD manual written by Claude, same size and structure as experiments/first-test/manual.md, frozen by sha256
18|  before any run. Why: otherwise the result can be blamed on the manual.
19|- Sandbox: the Keel v2-style profile + FreeCAD's own install readable; `import cadquery` / `OCP` blocked inside the
20|  answer run. Why: FreeCAD can run CadQuery; Glimmer could cheat by writing CadQuery.
21|- Arms (k = 1, one session each): **G** = Glimmer + FreeCAD manual + job; **S** = Spark Open (Baseten) + the same;
22|  **W** = Muse Wonder (`muse-wonder-1.0`, api.meta.ai, Meta credit) + the same, run **only on the jobs S failed**
23|  (decision, user 2026-10-29: "if Spark fails, it contacts Wonder to be helped"). **Teacher T** = jobs passed by S or
24|  by W after S failed. Why: shows whether an escalating teacher team can produce correct FreeCAD answers where Spark
25|  alone cannot. Privacy note: W sends the job + manual to Meta's API; in a real confidential deployment the escalation
26|  is switched off or uses a stronger open model; every record says which teacher made it.
27|- Every failure tagged: API error / crash (tool knowledge: training can fix) vs wrong geometry (general skill).
28|
29|## Free checks before any paid call
30|1. Claude hand-writes FreeCAD answers for 5 jobs: all PASS; 2 deliberately wrong answers FAIL.
31|2. The 30 CadQuery references round-trip through STEP (export → import) and still PASS against themselves.
32|3. Cheat test: an answer that imports cadquery is refused in the sandbox.
33|4. Neutral-text scan done and frozen (sha256).
34|
35|## Where answers run (decision, user 2026-10-29)
36|Nothing Glimmer or Spark writes runs on the user's Mac: every answer runs in a fresh Modal Sandbox (no network, no
37|answers inside, FreeCAD 1.1.4), and a separate cloud grader holds the references (SPEC §1-2). The Mac checks below were
38|done with Claude's hand-written answers only.
39|
40|## Free checks done (verified 2026-10-29, Claude; check commands run ad hoc in Claude's temp folder, not project code)
41|- FreeCAD 1.1.4 installed (`brew install --cask freecad`); headless `freecadcmd` builds a part and exports STEP in ~4 s
42|  (0.2 s warm); FreeCAD's own Python is 3.11.14 and has **no cadquery / OCP**.
43|- A FreeCAD part scored against a CadQuery reference: PASS at 0.2% and at 1e-6, mismatch 0.0.
44|- Hand-written FreeCAD answers (experiments/freecad/hand/): M1, M6, M10, H6, H13 all PASS at 0.2% and 1e-6;
45|  M1_wrong (hole 1 mm off) and H13_wrong (countersink too big) FAIL at both.
46|- The 30 CadQuery references survive a STEP round trip: 30/30 at 0.2% and 1e-6.
47|- Neutral-text scan of the 30 job texts (workplane, centered, cadquery, selector, >Z, sketch, extrude, cbore, csk…): none.
48|- Sandbox: freecadcmd runs under `env -i HOME=<scratch>` + sandbox-exec with experiments/freecad/sandbox_fc.reference.sb
49|  (Keel-v2 style, home + temp reads denied, writes only to scratch); inside it `import cadquery` → ModuleNotFoundError and
50|  reading experiments/first-test/expected.json → PermissionError.
51|- Manual: experiments/freecad/manual.md, an excerpt of FreeCAD's official "Topological data scripting" guide + the
52|  built-in Part `help()` text, 21,640 chars (CadQuery manual 21,696). 27 of its 30 official code examples run as
53|  written (3 doc quirks: a placeholder `myShape`, a missing `from math import radians`, one example OCC error); kept
54|  authentic. **Frozen: sha256 865ab9af45eb2fb554f97155fa8f3cf44f92d54973437a1f94c78d67cdc89bb6.**
55|
56|## Decision rule (pre-registered; reuses the Oct 28 day-1 gate; n = 30 at k = 1 ≈ ±17 points, act only on clear margins)
57|Revised after the verifier's check (forge-freecad-2026-10-29, READY WITH 3 EDITS), before any paid call:
58|1. **T < 70% → RUN INVALID for FreeCAD: stay on CadQuery.** No manual fix on exam failures (that would tune the manual on
59|   the exam). A manual fix is allowed only after a new user approval and is tested on the dry jobs D1-D3 only.
60|   Why: re-running after fixing the manual on exam failures re-touches the exam and biases the result.
61|2. G ≤ 60% AND T ≥ 75% AND T − G ≥ 20 points AND ≥ 8 jobs pass in T but not in G → **FreeCAD becomes the factory target**
62|   (teacher = Spark with Wonder escalation). S alone and W's rescues are reported separately.
63|3. G ≥ 75% → stay on hard CadQuery jobs.
64|4. Otherwise (grey zone) → **default: stay on CadQuery.** FreeCAD only if api_error ≥ 60% of G's FAILs AND ≥ 6 jobs pass
65|   in T but not in G. No re-run of only the differing jobs (selecting on the outcome shrinks the gap by regression).
66|   Why: the grey zone also decides whether to go above the $30 cap, so it must be a fixed rule, not a judgement call.
67|5. **Rules 1-4 are evaluated twice: on T and on S alone, and both are reported** (verifier edit A2,
68|   forge-freecad-escalation-2026-10-29). If they disagree, the report says "FreeCAD target only with Wonder escalation
69|   (closed API)" and the user decides. The report also gives Wonder's share of T's passes. S's INVALID (cut-off) jobs
70|   are NOT escalated; they stay INVALID. Why: T gives each job two tries by two models against G's one (a pass@2 effect
71|   that leans towards "FreeCAD target"), and every Wonder rescue sends the job to a closed API, which weakens the
72|   "private" claim; the user must see when the decision rests on that.
73|Failure tags: api_error = the answer raised, timed out, hit the memory limit or a PermissionError; wrong_geometry =
74|built but failed the checker, or `result` was not a Part solid; cut off by the token limit = INVALID (as the baseline).
75|Honest caveat for the report: FreeCAD's Part API has no counterbore/slot/polar-pattern helpers (CadQuery has them), so
76|part of a G-vs-S gap measures that the tool is harder to use, which is exactly the kind of difficulty a company tool has.
77|Manual note (not changed, hash frozen): its line "Part.show() is not available" is inaccurate (it exists headless);
78|harmless.
79|
80|## Money
81|Muse Code build ≈ $1.2-1.5; Glimmer 30 answers ≈ $1 (cold start + run); Spark 30 answers ≈ $0.7; Wonder only on S's
82|failures ≈ $0.10 each (≈ $0.5-2; worst case 16k output tokens ≈ $0.34 per call); cloud sandboxes + grader ≈ $0.1.
83|- decision (Claude, 2026-10-29, following the existing accounting where Muse Code's Meta-credit spend is already in the
84|  Forge total): **Meta credit for W counts INSIDE Forge's $30 (or $35) budget.** Why: one budget total, so the user's
85|  "go above $30?" decision sees every dollar.
86|- Caps for the test run: Modal + Baseten **$3.50** (session cap via experiments/common/run_session.sh, Baseten guard)
87|  + Meta (W) **$3** (`--budget-w`) = **$6.50 worst case**, plus the Muse build.
88|- Typical total ≈ $4.2 (build ≈ $1.35 + run ≈ $2.8); Forge total after ≈ $24 typical, ≈ $28 worst case.
89|  The full plan after the test (factory ≈ $5, training ≈ $4, final ≈ $1.5) ≈ $34-35 → needs the user's budget answer.
90|
91|## After the test
92|The gap test shows only room. "The factory works across tools" needs a trained result: train the tool with the bigger
93|gap; for the other tool, run the factory up to verified training data on screen without training.
94|In parallel (free): market evidence for Impact with the user's two problem frameworks.

1|# Fix spec for Muse Code: training pipeline (verifier NO-GO, report forge-train-pipeline-2026-10-29)
2|
3|Status: written by Claude 2026-10-29; needs the user's yes before Muse Code runs. Same rules as MUSE_SPEC.md (edit only
4|files in experiments/train/ and experiments/common/; never open blind/, experiments/option-a/ or expected*.json
5|contents EXCEPT that the exam guard in item 3 may read experiments/first-test/jobs.py texts and use
6|experiments/first-test/expected.json through code, without printing it; no network, no Modal runs, no commit).
7|
8|1. **Training loop (forge_train.py ~303-365):** count MICRO-steps (one example each) and OPTIMIZER steps separately:
9|   total optimizer steps = ceil(n_examples × epochs / grad_accum); loop over epochs × examples, call opt.step() every
10|   grad_accum micro-steps and once more at the end for a leftover partial group. `max_steps` limits OPTIMIZER steps.
11|   Record peak GPU memory AFTER the first opt.step() (when AdamW state exists) and stop then if > 76 GB. Put the
12|   schedule logic in a pure function (no torch) and test it offline: 400 examples, 2 epochs, accum 8 → 100 optimizer
13|   steps using all 800 micro-steps; 16 examples, 1 epoch → 2 steps; 8 examples with max_steps 10 and accum 1 → 10 steps.
14|2. **Data reaches Modal:** the local entrypoint reads the local JSONL (and also accepts a JSON array, as
15|   experiments/smoke/smoke_examples.json is), validates each record has "text" and "code", and passes the records
16|   themselves (a list of dicts) to train.remote(), not a path. Test both input formats.
17|3. **Exam guard (local, before any remote call):** refuse to train if any training record (a) has text with
18|   normalized similarity ≥ 0.8 to any of the 33 first-test job texts (difflib ratio after lowercasing and collapsing
19|   numbers to a placeholder is fine, and also exact-number comparison), or (b) when its code is built, matches an exam
20|   reference part at 1e-6 (use experiments/common/score_one.py logic against each job's reference build from
21|   experiments/first-test/jobs.py, in the sandbox). Save the guard report to results/train-<out>/exam_guard.json (counts
22|   only, no reference values). Test with a fake exam set.
23|4. **Timeouts from the money cap:** apply the planned timeouts with `.with_options(timeout=...)` (or equivalent) at call
24|   time; `gpu_minutes` and `--cap-dollars` must really bound each function; subtract earlier spend in the same
25|   entrypoint run (train → merge → serve share one cap). Test that a cap of $1.50 gives timeouts whose worst-case total
26|   cost ≤ $1.50.
27|5. **Log what the model is trained on:** train_log.json gets the fully rendered first training example (prompt +
28|   answer) and the first 40 decoded tokens that carry loss, so we can see exactly which tokens are learned.
29|6. **serve_merged:** stop using it for scoring; keep it only for a quick format check (one prompt, ≤ 3 min after ready,
30|   overall timeout from the cap). Final-exam scoring will use the existing runner (separate spec later).
31|7. **run_session.sh:** `trap ... EXIT INT TERM HUP`; run each runner call in its own process group and kill that group
32|   in the trap; the trap always runs `modal app stop forge-glimmer -y` and prints whether it stopped. Test with a dummy
33|   runner command that sleeps, sending TERM to the script.
34|8. **Budget reserve:** budget_left gets a `--reserve` (default $0.30) subtracted before handing a budget to a runner
35|   call, because the runner's guard stops only NEW calls and in-flight answers still cost money.
36|Run `~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/train experiments/common` until all pass. Short report:
37|files changed, the pytest line, anything not followed.
38|
39|## Spec edits from the verifier's spec check (forge-train-fixspec-2026-10-29, READY WITH 5 SPEC EDITS) — binding
40|1. **Deadline inside train (item 4, A6):** train() gets `deadline_s` = its timeout minus 240 s. When the time left falls
41|   below that margin, it stops after the current optimizer step and saves the adapter and train_log.json (marked
42|   `stopped_at_deadline`). It also saves the adapter every 25 optimizer steps. Split the cap as: merge 12 min H100 +
43|   serve 6 min A100 reserved first, the rest to train. Refuse if train gets under 15 min.
44|2. **Exam guard refusals (item 3a, A3):** refuse a record only if (i) its exact-number text ratio is ≥ 0.9 to an exam
45|   text, or (ii) its built part matches an exam part. Number-collapsed ratios ≥ 0.8 are counted in exam_guard.json as
46|   warnings, not refusals. Drop refused records, and abort only if more than 5% are refused.
47|3. **Exam guard building (item 3b, A4):** build the 33 references in-process with jobs.py (trusted code); run only the
48|   training record's code in the sandbox. Compare bbox and volume first (1e-6) and run the full score only on a match.
49|4. **Startup in the cost (item 4, A7):** set `startup_timeout` explicitly (e.g. 600 s) on each function and include it in
50|   the worst-case cost: (startup + timeout) × rate ≤ cap.
51|5. **Trap that really fires (item 7, A10):** start each runner call in the background (`cmd & RPID=$!; wait $RPID`) so
52|   the trap can run. In the trap, kill the runner and its children (`kill -TERM $RPID; pkill -TERM -P $RPID`; macOS has
53|   no setsid). Then run `modal app stop`. The TERM test must show the dummy runner dead and "app stopped" printed.
54|Also (cheap, same session): LR schedule and logs per optimizer step, the partial last group scaled by its real size (A2);
55|epochs = 2 in the max_steps test (A1); `--spent-dollars` to carry earlier spend (A8); upload data to the volume when it
56|is over 5 MB (A9); the smoke entrypoint uses the same loader (A11).
57|
58|## Round 2 (verifier re-check forge-train-pipeline-recheck-2026-10-29, GO WITH 2 FIXES) — binding
59|1. **Launchable (WRONG finding):** the local entrypoints call `.remote()` outside a running app. Wrap the remote part of
60|   each entrypoint in `with modal.enable_output(): with app.run():`, so `python experiments/train/forge_train.py smoke
61|   --cap-dollars X` works from the forge venv (modal will be installed there, user's call). Why: without it the paid
62|   smoke/full runs cannot start at all. Add a free test: `smoke --cap-dollars 2.0` prints CAP REFUSED without any remote
63|   call. The test must monkeypatch `app.run`, `modal.enable_output` and every `.remote()` to raise if called, so a wrong
64|   cap check fails the test instead of starting a paid H100 job. Why: with item 2 the minimum cap is ≈ $2.89, so $3.0
65|   would NOT be refused, and with modal now installed an unguarded test could really launch (verifier, urgent note).
66|   Free CLI check Claude runs after the build: `python experiments/train/forge_train.py smoke --cap-dollars 2.0` →
67|   prints CAP REFUSED and exits with code 2.
68|2. **Minimum cap:** set `STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S = 300` (minimum total cap ≈ $2.89 instead of $3.77). Why: with 600 s a $3
69|   training cap is refused (train gets only 206 s).
70|3. **Fail closed:** if the exam guard cannot build an exam reference, raise (no silent pass). Why: a fail-open guard could
71|   let an exam copy into training and invalidate the final exam.
72|4. **serve_merged:** its wait (ready ≤ 3 min) + one prompt must fit inside its timeout; make the request timeout ≤ 120 s.
73|5. Docstring + README line: "never `modal run forge_train.py::train`; it bypasses the exam guard and the money cap".

1|# Spec for Muse Code: FreeCAD gap-test runner (arms G and S) — needs verifier check + user yes
2|
3|Status: written by Claude 2026-10-29 (user: "install FreeCAD, check how it works, plan all for the paid run"). Plan and
4|free-check evidence: experiments/freecad/PLAN.md. Every item says why it matters.
5|
6|## Rules
7|- Work in ~/projects/forge; new files only in experiments/freecad/ (do not edit experiments/first-test/, which is frozen:
8|  import from it instead). Never open blind/ folders, experiments/option-a/, or the contents of expected*.json.
9|- No network, no model calls, no Modal runs, no commit, never print keys.
10|- Tests: `~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/freecad` until all pass. Sandbox tests may skip
11|  inside your shell; Claude re-runs them outside.
12|
13|## 1. Cloud safety box: `cloud_exec.py` (decision, user 2026-10-29: nothing Glimmer writes may run on the Mac)
14|Every answer runs in a **fresh Modal Sandbox** (`modal.Sandbox.create`, https://modal.com/docs/sdk/py/latest/Sandbox):
15|`block_network=True`, no secrets, no volumes, cpu 1, memory (1024, 4096) MiB, `timeout` 90 s, one sandbox per answer,
16|terminated after use. Image: FreeCAD **1.1.4** for Linux from the official release asset `FreeCAD_1.1.4-Linux-x86_64-py311.AppImage` (GitHub
17|release 2026-09-28): download it in the image build, verify its SHA256 against the release's SHA256 file, unpack with
18|`--appimage-extract` (no FUSE needed), and the build must print `freecadcmd` version 1.1.4 (the Mac manual's version).
19|No conda route: conda-forge has no 1.1.4 build (verifier, anaconda.org API: 1.1.0, 1.1.3, 2026.09.16). Why: a different
20|FreeCAD version could make the manual inaccurate and change the result. The image contains ONLY FreeCAD + `run_one_fc.py`: no references, no jobs file, no expected.json, no cadquery.
21|Steps: write `answer.py` with `sb.filesystem.write_text`, run `freecadcmd /work/run_one_fc.py` with `sb.exec`
22|(env FC_SCRATCH=/work), read back `/work/answer.step` (bytes) and `/work/measure.json`, then `sb.terminate()`. Run the answer with `sb.exec(..., timeout=60)` inside the 90 s box (the baseline's 60 s
23|limit, so speed limits stay the same); refuse a STEP larger than 20 MB. The verdict and failure tags come only from the
24|grader; the box's measure.json is for logs only (why: the box runs untrusted code and must not decide its own score).
25|Why: the box never holds the answers, has no internet and is new for each answer, so an answer cannot read the
26|answer key, other jobs' results, or anything on the user's Mac.
27|`run_one_fc.py` (inside the box): exec answer.py with `ns = {"__name__": "__main__"}`; require `result` to be a
28|`Part.Shape` with ≥ 1 solid (`ERROR: no variable named 'result'` / `ERROR: result is not a Part solid`); refuse
29|`import cadquery` / `OCP` with an import hook; write answer.step + measure.json (bbox, volume, solids, isValid).
30|
31|## 2. Cloud grader: `cloud_grade.py`
32|A separate Modal Function (CPU, our own trusted code) with CadQuery 2.8 + experiments/first-test/{jobs.py,checks.py,
33|expected.json} baked into its image. Input: job id + STEP bytes; output: verdict at 0.2% (the verdict) and at 1e-6,
34|the failed checks, measurements. It never runs model code. Why: the reference parts live only here, never in the box.
35|**Consistency check before any paid run (CPU only, cents):** (a) run all 7 hand answers of experiments/freecad/hand/
36|IN the cloud box → 5 PASS + 2 FAIL through the cloud grader, exactly as on the Mac, with bbox and volume within 1e-9
37|relative of the Mac-made parts; (b) the 30 CadQuery references through the cloud grader → 30/30 PASS. Why: (a) tests
38|the Linux FreeCAD box itself, (b) tests the grader; together they show the cloud gives the same verdicts as the Mac.
39|
40|## 2b. Mac side
41|runner_fc.py imports `modal` to create sandboxes and call the grader, so modal must be installed in the forge venv
42|(`~/projects/forge/.venv`); this is the user's decision (the same one as the training fix). Muse Code must not install
43|anything; if modal is missing, tests that need it skip and the CLI exits with a clear message.
44|
45|## 3. `runner_fc.py` (reuses the frozen first-test runner; do not copy-paste its logic)
46|Import from experiments/first-test/runner.py: the Glimmer/Baseten request code and retry, code extraction, the budget
47|guard, k and workers handling. Replace only:
48|- system prompt: "You write FreeCAD Python code using the Part module (import FreeCAD as App, Part). Units are
49|  millimetres. Assign the final solid (a Part.Shape) to a variable named result. Reply with exactly one Python code
50|  block and nothing else." Why: the same instruction as the CadQuery system prompt, tool swapped.
51|- manual: experiments/freecad/manual.md, refused if its sha256 differs from the value frozen in PLAN.md
52|  (865ab9af45eb2fb554f97155fa8f3cf44f92d54973437a1f94c78d67cdc89bb6). Why: a changed manual changes the result.
53|- user message: "Here is the FreeCAD manual. Use it.\n\n" + manual + "\n\n" + job text (same layout as arm B).
54|- answer execution: `cloud_exec.py` (Modal Sandbox) → STEP bytes → `cloud_grade.py` (Modal Function): **0.2% is the
55|  verdict** (the baseline's yardstick) and 1e-6 is also recorded. Nothing from the model runs on the Mac; the Mac only
56|  coordinates and writes logs. Run up to 8 sandboxes in parallel.
57|- arms: `G` = Glimmer (same body as arm B: max_tokens 16000, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64); `S` = Spark Open
58|  on Baseten (meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026, same sampling, header x-session-affinity, log cached_tokens); `W` = Muse
59|  Wonder (`muse-wonder-1.0`, https://api.meta.ai/v1 chat completions, key from env META_KEY, same messages, max_tokens
60|  16000; reasoning tokens are billed as output) run only on job ids that FAILED in S's calls.jsonl (`--escalate-from <S
61|  run dir>`), with its own budget guard (`--budget-w`, $20/M output, $4/M input, $0.20/M cached). k = 1. Summary adds
62|  T = S ∪ W-rescues per job and evaluates the PLAN rules 1-4 on BOTH T and S alone (PLAN rule 5); if they disagree,
63|  report.md says "FreeCAD target only with Wonder escalation (closed API)"; it also gives Wonder's share of T's passes.
64|  S's INVALID (cut-off) jobs are not escalated. Before the W arm runs on failures, `--w-smoke` sends ONE call (dry job

7|## Question

9|Spark Open + the same manual? If so, FreeCAD is the factory's training target (a bigger, more visible gain).

13|  centring hints) and made neutral before freezing. Why: CadQuery words would push the model toward CadQuery.

15|  reads ONLY that path and scores it with experiments/first-test/checks.py at 0.2% (same yardstick as the baseline),
16|  1e-6 also reported. Why: no new exam = no new exam bugs.

18|  before any run. Why: otherwise the result can be blamed on the manual.

20|  answer run. Why: FreeCAD can run CadQuery; Glimmer could cheat by writing CadQuery.

22|  **W** = Muse Wonder (`muse-wonder-1.0`, api.meta.ai, Meta credit) + the same, run **only on the jobs S failed**

24|  by W after S failed. Why: shows whether an escalating teacher team can produce correct FreeCAD answers where Spark
25|  alone cannot. Privacy note: W sends the job + manual to Meta's API; in a real confidential deployment the escalation
26|  is switched off or uses a stronger open model; every record says which teacher made it.

62|   smoke/full runs cannot start at all. Add a free test: `smoke --cap-dollars 2.0` prints CAP REFUSED without any remote
63|   call. The test must monkeypatch `app.run`, `modal.enable_output` and every `.remote()` to raise if called, so a wrong
64|   cap check fails the test instead of starting a paid H100 job. Why: with item 2 the minimum cap is ≈ $2.89, so $3.0
65|   would NOT be refused, and with modal now installed an unguarded test could really launch (verifier, urgent note).

251|def plan_optimizer_steps(n_examples, epochs, grad_accum, max_steps=None):

254|    Loops epochs x examples; an optimizer step fires every grad_accum
255|    micro-steps, plus once more at the end for a leftover partial group.
256|    `max_steps` caps OPTIMIZER steps. Returns {"micro_steps",
257|    "optimizer_steps", "groups"} where groups lists each optimizer step's
258|    micro-step count (the last may be a smaller partial group).
259|    """
260|    if grad_accum < 1:
261|        raise ValueError("grad_accum must be >= 1")
262|    total_micro = max(0, int(n_examples)) * max(0, int(epochs))
263|    full = total_micro // grad_accum
264|    groups = [grad_accum] * full
265|    leftover = total_micro - full * grad_accum
266|    if leftover:
267|        groups.append(leftover)
268|    if max_steps is not None:
269|        groups = groups[:max(0, int(max_steps))]

328|def text_ratios(text, exam_text):
329|    """(exact_ratio, collapsed_ratio) of a training text vs an exam text."""
330|    exact = difflib.SequenceMatcher(
331|        None, normalize_exact(text), normalize_exact(exam_text)).ratio()
332|    collapsed = difflib.SequenceMatcher(

342|    warn (counted, not refused) when a number-collapsed ratio is >= 0.8.
343|    `exam_texts` is injectable so tests can use a fake exam set.
344|    """
345|    best_exact, best_collapsed = 0.0, 0.0
346|    for exam in exam_texts:
347|        exact, collapsed = text_ratios(text, exam)
348|        best_exact = max(best_exact, exact)
349|        best_collapsed = max(best_collapsed, collapsed)
350|    detail = {"exact_ratio": round(best_exact, 4),
351|              "collapsed_ratio": round(best_collapsed, 4)}

175|def default_plan(cap_dollars, train_s=14 * 60, merge_s=10 * 60, serve_s=10 * 60):

187|def plan_timeouts(cap_dollars, steps, startup_s=0, spent_dollars=0.0):
188|    """Derive each Modal function's timeout from the money left.
189|
190|    `steps` is a list of (name, rate_per_hour, want_seconds), charged in
191|    order. `startup_s` is the Modal startup allowance per function: the
192|    worst-case cost of a step is (startup_s + want) * rate, and that is
193|    what must fit in the money left. `spent_dollars` carries earlier spend
194|    in the same entrypoint run (train -> merge -> serve share one cap).
195|    Returns {name: seconds} plus `_left`. Raises CapExceeded when a step
196|    does not fit in the money left (refuses to start it).
197|    """
198|    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
199|    out = {}
200|    for name, rate, want in steps:
201|        cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + want, rate)
202|        if cost > left:
203|            raise CapExceeded(
204|                "step %r wants %ds + %ds startup ($%.2f at $%.2f/h) but only "
205|                "$%.2f is left of the $%.2f cap; refusing to start it"
206|                % (name, want, startup_s, cost, rate, left, cap_dollars)
207|            )
208|        out[name] = want
209|        left -= cost
210|    out["_left"] = round(left, 2)
211|    return out

214|def split_cap(cap_dollars, spent_dollars=0.0, startup_s=STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S):
215|    """Reserve merge + serve first, hand the rest to train.
216|
217|    Merge gets 12 min H100, serve 6 min A100; train gets whatever the cap
218|    still covers (startup included). Refuses (CapExceeded) when train
219|    would get under 15 min. Returns {train, merge, serve, startup_s}.
220|    """
221|    merge_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + MERGE_RESERVE_S, H100_RATE)
222|    serve_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + SERVE_RESERVE_S, A100_RATE)
223|    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
224|    if merge_cost + serve_cost > left:
225|        raise CapExceeded(
226|            "cap $%.2f (spent $%.2f) cannot reserve merge $%.2f + serve "
227|            "$%.2f; refusing" % (cap_dollars, spent_dollars or 0.0,
228|                                 merge_cost, serve_cost)
229|        )
230|    train_budget = left - merge_cost - serve_cost
231|    train_s = train_budget * 3600.0 / H100_RATE - startup_s
232|    if train_s < MIN_TRAIN_S:
233|        raise CapExceeded(
234|            "cap $%.2f leaves only %ds for train (under %ds); refusing"
235|            % (cap_dollars, max(0, int(train_s)), MIN_TRAIN_S)
236|        )
237|    return {"train": int(train_s), "merge": MERGE_RESERVE_S,
238|            "serve": SERVE_RESERVE_S, "startup_s": startup_s}

241|def worst_case_cost(plan, rates, startup_s=0):
242|    """Worst-case total $ of a timeout plan: sum of (startup + t) * rate."""
243|    total = 0.0
244|    for name, seconds in plan.items():
245|        if name.startswith("_"):
246|            continue
247|        total += dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + seconds, rates[name])
248|    return total

251|def plan_optimizer_steps(n_examples, epochs, grad_accum, max_steps=None):
252|    """Pure schedule: MICRO-steps (one example each) vs OPTIMIZER steps.
253|
254|    Loops epochs x examples; an optimizer step fires every grad_accum
255|    micro-steps, plus once more at the end for a leftover partial group.
256|    `max_steps` caps OPTIMIZER steps. Returns {"micro_steps",
257|    "optimizer_steps", "groups"} where groups lists each optimizer step's
258|    micro-step count (the last may be a smaller partial group).
259|    """
260|    if grad_accum < 1:
261|        raise ValueError("grad_accum must be >= 1")
262|    total_micro = max(0, int(n_examples)) * max(0, int(epochs))
263|    full = total_micro // grad_accum
264|    groups = [grad_accum] * full
265|    leftover = total_micro - full * grad_accum
266|    if leftover:
267|        groups.append(leftover)
268|    if max_steps is not None:
269|        groups = groups[:max(0, int(max_steps))]
270|    return {"micro_steps": sum(groups),
271|            "optimizer_steps": len(groups),
272|            "groups": groups}

305|# Local guard, run BEFORE any remote call. Text side: difflib ratio after
306|# lowercasing; exact-number ratios >= 0.9 refuse, number-collapsed ratios
307|# >= 0.8 warn. Code side: the exam references are built in-process with
308|# experiments/first-test/jobs.py (trusted code); only the training
309|# record's code runs in the sandbox. bbox + volume are compared first at
310|# 1e-6 and the full score runs only on a match. Refused records are
311|# dropped; the run aborts only when more than 5% are refused. The saved
312|# report holds counts only, never reference values.

314|_NUM_RE = re.compile(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?")
315|_NUM_TOKEN = " #NUM "

318|def normalize_exact(text):
319|    """Lowercased text with numbers kept (for the refusal ratio)."""
320|    return (text or "").lower()
321|
322|
323|def normalize_collapsed(text):
324|    """Lowercased text with every number replaced by a placeholder."""
325|    return _NUM_RE.sub(_NUM_TOKEN, (text or "").lower())

328|def text_ratios(text, exam_text):
329|    """(exact_ratio, collapsed_ratio) of a training text vs an exam text."""
330|    exact = difflib.SequenceMatcher(
331|        None, normalize_exact(text), normalize_exact(exam_text)).ratio()
332|    collapsed = difflib.SequenceMatcher(
333|        None, normalize_collapsed(text),
334|        normalize_collapsed(exam_text)).ratio()
335|    return exact, collapsed

338|def check_text_record(text, exam_texts):
339|    """Classify one record's text: ("refuse"|"warn"|"ok", detail dict).
340|
341|    Refuse when the exact-number ratio to any exam text is >= 0.9;
342|    warn (counted, not refused) when a number-collapsed ratio is >= 0.8.
343|    `exam_texts` is injectable so tests can use a fake exam set.
344|    """
345|    best_exact, best_collapsed = 0.0, 0.0
346|    for exam in exam_texts:
347|        exact, collapsed = text_ratios(text, exam)
348|        best_exact = max(best_exact, exact)
349|        best_collapsed = max(best_collapsed, collapsed)
350|    detail = {"exact_ratio": round(best_exact, 4),
351|              "collapsed_ratio": round(best_collapsed, 4)}
352|    if best_exact >= EXAM_REFUSE_RATIO:
353|        return "refuse", detail
354|    if best_collapsed >= EXAM_WARN_RATIO:
355|        return "warn", detail
356|    return "ok", detail

359|def measurements_match(m, e, tol=EXAM_TOL):
360|    """Prefilter: bbox faces and volume agree within tol (default 1e-6)."""
361|    try:
362|        if abs(m["volume"] - e["volume"]) > tol:
363|            return False
364|        return all(abs(a - b) <= tol for a, b in zip(m["bbox"], e["bbox"]))
365|    except (KeyError, TypeError):
366|        return False

372|    bbox + volume are compared first at tol; the full score runs only on
373|    a prefilter hit. `full_score_fn(train_meas, ref_meas)` defaults to a
374|    strict pass (prefilter decides); pass the checks.score-based scorer
375|    for the real decision. Returns (matched, job_index or None).

377|    for i, ref in enumerate(ref_meases):

382|        try:

2|# Glimmer evaluation session with a whole-session cap (generalised run_session_v2.sh).
3|# One deploy of deploy/modal_glimmer.py, wait for ready, run the given runner
4|# commands one after another, each with --budget = money LEFT =
5|# cap - GPU time since deploy x $2.50/h minus the $0.30 reserve (refuse to
6|# start when <= $0.05), optional pilot + GO/STOP file pause, always stops the
7|# app and prints whether it stopped.
8|# Arms/jobs/k are parameters (not hard-coded): each RUN spec is
9|#   "<jobs>:<out-subdir>:<arms>:<k>"   (e.g. "main:main-BR:BR:1").
10|# Usage: run_session.sh <absolute-out-dir> [cap-$] [--pilot <jobs>:<subdir>:<arms>:<k>] [--run <jobs>:<subdir>:<arms>:<k> ...]
11|# Default runs mirror the step-2 baseline: pilot dry/BR,BX/k=1, then main BR/k=1 and main B2,BX/k=3.
12|#
13|# Each runner call starts in the background (cmd & RPID=$!; wait $RPID) so
14|# the EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP trap can always run. The trap kills the runner and
15|# its children (kill -TERM $RPID; pkill -TERM -P $RPID; macOS has no setsid),
16|# then always runs `modal app stop forge-glimmer -y` and prints whether it
17|# stopped.
18|#
19|# Offline-test seams (env, all optional; production defaults unchanged):
20|#   RUN_SESSION_RUNNER_CMD  full runner command prefix instead of runner.py
21|#                           (e.g. "sleep 300" for the TERM test)
22|#   RUN_SESSION_SKIP_DEPLOY=1  skip secret/deploy/ready, pretend URL=skip
23|#   MODAL_BIN               modal binary (default "modal"; stub it in tests)

1|"""Strict single-answer check: score one reply against a reference program.
2|
3|Given a reply text (or a file holding it) and a reference CadQuery program
4|(file), extracts the code, runs it in the sandbox (runner.run_code with
5|experiments/b2-hint/sandbox_cq.sb), and scores it with
6|experiments/first-test/checks.py at TOL_DIFF = 1e-6. Prints PASS or FAIL
7|with reasons.
8|
9|Usage: score_one.py [--reply-file PATH | <reply text>] <reference program file>
10|       score_one.py --reply-file reply.txt --reference ref.py [--sandbox-dir DIR]
11|"""
12|import argparse
13|import os
14|import sys
15|
16|HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
17|FORGE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))

26|)
27|
28|STRICT_TOL_DIFF = 1e-6
29|
30|
31|def read_reply(reply=None, reply_file=None):
32|    """Reply text, from --reply-file or from the argument (a path or text)."""
33|    if reply_file:
34|        with open(reply_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
35|            return f.read()
36|    if reply is not None and os.path.isfile(reply):
37|        with open(reply, encoding="utf-8") as f:
38|            return f.read()
39|    return reply or ""
40|
41|
42|def run_reference_program(path):
43|    """Execute the reference program file; returns (shape, error)."""
44|    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
45|        src = f.read()
46|    code = runner.extract_code(src)
47|    if not code or not code.strip():
48|        code = src
49|    return code, src
50|
51|
52|def score_reply(reply_text, ref_path, sandbox_dir=None, timeout=None):
53|    """Score one reply. Returns (passed, reasons list, measurements)."""
54|    old_tol = checks.TOL_DIFF
55|    checks.TOL_DIFF = STRICT_TOL_DIFF
56|    try:
57|        code = runner.extract_code(reply_text)
58|        if not code or not code.strip():
59|            return False, ["empty reply"], None
60|        shape, err = runner.run_code(
61|            code,
62|            timeout=timeout or runner.RUN_TIMEOUT,
63|            sandbox_profile=SANDBOX_PROFILE,
64|            sandbox_dir=sandbox_dir,
65|        )
66|        if shape is None:
67|            return False, ["did not run: %s" % (err or "code error")], None
68|        ref_code, _ = run_reference_program(ref_path)
69|        ref_shape, ref_err = runner.run_code(
70|            ref_code,
71|            timeout=timeout or runner.RUN_TIMEOUT,
72|            sandbox_profile=SANDBOX_PROFILE,
73|            sandbox_dir=sandbox_dir,
74|        )
75|        if ref_shape is None:
76|            return False, ["reference did not run: %s" % (ref_err or "code error")], None
77|        expected = {k: checks.measure(ref_shape)[k]
78|                    for k in ("bbox", "volume", "area", "com")}
79|        passed, fails, m = checks.score(shape, ref_shape, expected)
80|        return passed, list(fails), m
81|    finally:
82|        checks.TOL_DIFF = old_tol

87|    parser.add_argument("reply", nargs="?",
88|                        help="reply text, or a path to a file holding it")
89|    parser.add_argument("ref", nargs="?", help="reference CadQuery program file")
90|    parser.add_argument("--reply-file", default=None,
91|                        help="file holding the reply (overrides the reply arg)")
92|    parser.add_argument("--reference", default=None,
93|                        help="reference program file (overrides the ref arg)")
94|    parser.add_argument("--sandbox-dir", default=None)
95|    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
96|    reply_text = read_reply(args.reply, args.reply_file)
97|    reference = args.reference or args.ref
98|    if not reference:
99|        parser.error("a reference CadQuery program file is required")
100|    if not os.path.isfile(reference):
101|        parser.error("reference file not found: %s" % reference)
102|    passed, reasons, _ = score_reply(
103|        reply_text, reference, sandbox_dir=args.sandbox_dir)
104|    if passed:
105|        print("PASS")
106|        return 0
107|    print("FAIL %s" % ("; ".join(reasons) if reasons else "checks failed"))
108|    return 1

1|#!/bin/zsh
2|# Glimmer evaluation session with a whole-session cap (generalised run_session_v2.sh).
3|# One deploy of deploy/modal_glimmer.py, wait for ready, run the given runner
4|# commands one after another, each with --budget = money LEFT =
5|# cap - GPU time since deploy x $2.50/h minus the $0.30 reserve (refuse to
6|# start when <= $0.05), optional pilot + GO/STOP file pause, always stops the
7|# app and prints whether it stopped.
8|# Arms/jobs/k are parameters (not hard-coded): each RUN spec is
9|#   "<jobs>:<out-subdir>:<arms>:<k>"   (e.g. "main:main-BR:BR:1").
10|# Usage: run_session.sh <absolute-out-dir> [cap-$] [--pilot <jobs>:<subdir>:<arms>:<k>] [--run <jobs>:<subdir>:<arms>:<k> ...]
11|# Default runs mirror the step-2 baseline: pilot dry/BR,BX/k=1, then main BR/k=1 and main B2,BX/k=3.
12|#
13|# Each runner call starts in the background (cmd & RPID=$!; wait $RPID) so
14|# the EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP trap can always run. The trap kills the runner and
15|# its children (kill -TERM $RPID; pkill -TERM -P $RPID; macOS has no setsid),
16|# then always runs `modal app stop forge-glimmer -y` and prints whether it
17|# stopped.
18|#
19|# Offline-test seams (env, all optional; production defaults unchanged):
20|#   RUN_SESSION_RUNNER_CMD  full runner command prefix instead of runner.py
21|#                           (e.g. "sleep 300" for the TERM test)
22|#   RUN_SESSION_SKIP_DEPLOY=1  skip secret/deploy/ready, pretend URL=skip
23|#   MODAL_BIN               modal binary (default "modal"; stub it in tests)
24|set -u
25|OUT=$1; shift
26|CAP=3.0
27|case "${1:-}" in
28|  [0-9]* ) CAP=$1; shift;;
29|esac
30|PILOT="dry:pilot:BR,BX:1"
31|RUNS=()
32|while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
33|  case "$1" in
34|    --pilot) PILOT=$2; shift 2;;
35|    --run) RUNS+=("$2"); shift 2;;
36|    *) echo "unknown arg $1"; exit 2;;
37|  esac
38|done
39|[ ${#RUNS[@]} -eq 0 ] && RUNS=("main:main-BR:BR:1" "main:main-B2BX:B2,BX:3")
40|mkdir -p "$OUT"

42|COMMON=~/projects/forge/experiments/common

1|"""Strict single-answer check: score one reply against a reference program.
2|
3|Given a reply text (or a file holding it) and a reference CadQuery program
4|(file), extracts the code, runs it in the sandbox (runner.run_code with
5|experiments/b2-hint/sandbox_cq.sb), and scores it with
6|experiments/first-test/checks.py at TOL_DIFF = 1e-6. Prints PASS or FAIL
7|with reasons.
8|
9|Usage: score_one.py [--reply-file PATH | <reply text>] <reference program file>
10|       score_one.py --reply-file reply.txt --reference ref.py [--sandbox-dir DIR]
11|"""
12|import argparse
13|import os
14|import sys
15|
16|HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
17|FORGE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
18|FT = os.path.join(FORGE, "experiments", "first-test")
19|if FT not in sys.path:
20|    sys.path.insert(0, FT)
21|import checks  # noqa: E402
22|import runner  # noqa: E402
23|
24|SANDBOX_PROFILE = os.path.join(
25|    FORGE, "experiments", "b2-hint", "sandbox_cq.sb"
26|)
27|
28|STRICT_TOL_DIFF = 1e-6
29|
30|
31|def read_reply(reply=None, reply_file=None):
32|    """Reply text, from --reply-file or from the argument (a path or text)."""
33|    if reply_file:
34|        with open(reply_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
35|            return f.read()
36|    if reply is not None and os.path.isfile(reply):
37|        with open(reply, encoding="utf-8") as f:
38|            return f.read()
39|    return reply or ""
40|
41|
42|def run_reference_program(path):
43|    """Execute the reference program file; returns (shape, error)."""
44|    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
45|        src = f.read()
46|    code = runner.extract_code(src)
47|    if not code or not code.strip():
48|        code = src
49|    return code, src
50|
51|
52|def score_reply(reply_text, ref_path, sandbox_dir=None, timeout=None):
53|    """Score one reply. Returns (passed, reasons list, measurements)."""
54|    old_tol = checks.TOL_DIFF
55|    checks.TOL_DIFF = STRICT_TOL_DIFF
56|    try:
57|        code = runner.extract_code(reply_text)
58|        if not code or not code.strip():
59|            return False, ["empty reply"], None
60|        shape, err = runner.run_code(
61|            code,
62|            timeout=timeout or runner.RUN_TIMEOUT,
63|            sandbox_profile=SANDBOX_PROFILE,
64|            sandbox_dir=sandbox_dir,
65|        )
66|        if shape is None:
67|            return False, ["did not run: %s" % (err or "code error")], None
68|        ref_code, _ = run_reference_program(ref_path)
69|        ref_shape, ref_err = runner.run_code(
70|            ref_code,
71|            timeout=timeout or runner.RUN_TIMEOUT,
72|            sandbox_profile=SANDBOX_PROFILE,
73|            sandbox_dir=sandbox_dir,
74|        )
75|        if ref_shape is None:
76|            return False, ["reference did not run: %s" % (ref_err or "code error")], None
77|        expected = {k: checks.measure(ref_shape)[k]
78|                    for k in ("bbox", "volume", "area", "com")}
79|        passed, fails, m = checks.score(shape, ref_shape, expected)
80|        return passed, list(fails), m
81|    finally:
82|        checks.TOL_DIFF = old_tol
83|
84|
85|def main(argv=None):
86|    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Strict single-answer check")
87|    parser.add_argument("reply", nargs="?",
88|                        help="reply text, or a path to a file holding it")
89|    parser.add_argument("ref", nargs="?", help="reference CadQuery program file")
90|    parser.add_argument("--reply-file", default=None,
91|                        help="file holding the reply (overrides the reply arg)")
92|    parser.add_argument("--reference", default=None,
93|                        help="reference program file (overrides the ref arg)")
94|    parser.add_argument("--sandbox-dir", default=None)
95|    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
96|    reply_text = read_reply(args.reply, args.reply_file)
97|    reference = args.reference or args.ref
98|    if not reference:
99|        parser.error("a reference CadQuery program file is required")
100|    if not os.path.isfile(reference):
101|        parser.error("reference file not found: %s" % reference)
102|    passed, reasons, _ = score_reply(
103|        reply_text, reference, sandbox_dir=args.sandbox_dir)
104|    if passed:
105|        print("PASS")
106|        return 0
107|    print("FAIL %s" % ("; ".join(reasons) if reasons else "checks failed"))
108|    return 1
109|
110|
111|if __name__ == "__main__":
112|    sys.exit(main())

1|"""Measure a CadQuery result and compare it with a job's expected values (PLAN.md section 6)."""
2|import cadquery as cq
3|
4|TOL_POS = 0.1      # mm, bounding-box faces
5|TOL_COM = 0.3      # mm, centre of mass
6|TOL_REL = 0.01     # 1 %, volume and surface area
7|TOL_DIFF = 0.002   # 0.2 % of the reference volume may differ (answer XOR reference); B-rep booleans are exact
8|
9|
10|def to_shape(result):
11|    if isinstance(result, cq.Workplane):
12|        vals = [v for v in result.vals() if isinstance(v, cq.Shape)]
13|        return vals[0] if len(vals) == 1 else cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
14|    if isinstance(result, cq.Assembly):
15|        return result.toCompound()
16|    return result
17|
18|
19|def measure(result):
20|    s = to_shape(result)
21|    bb = s.BoundingBox()
22|    com = cq.Shape.centerOfMass(s)
23|    return {
24|        "bbox": [round(v, 3) for v in (bb.xmin, bb.ymin, bb.zmin, bb.xmax, bb.ymax, bb.zmax)],
25|        "volume": round(s.Volume(), 3),
26|        "area": round(s.Area(), 3),
27|        "com": [round(com.x, 3), round(com.y, 3), round(com.z, 3)],
28|        "solids": len(s.Solids()),
29|        "valid": bool(s.isValid()),
30|    }
31|
32|
33|def compare(m, e):
34|    """Return the list of failed checks (empty list = PASS)."""
35|    fails = []
36|    if m["solids"] != 1:
37|        fails.append(f"solids={m['solids']}")
38|    if not m["valid"]:
39|        fails.append("invalid shape")
40|    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_POS for a, b in zip(m["bbox"], e["bbox"])):
41|        fails.append("bbox")
42|    for k in ("volume", "area"):
43|        if abs(m[k] - e[k]) > TOL_REL * abs(e[k]):
44|            fails.append(k)
45|    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_COM for a, b in zip(m["com"], e["com"])):
46|        fails.append("com")
47|    return fails
48|
49|
50|def mismatch(answer, reference):
51|    """Volume that is in one part but not the other, as a fraction of the reference volume.
52|    Catches any moved feature, even symmetric moves that keep size, volume, area and centre of mass."""
53|    a, r = to_shape(answer), to_shape(reference)
54|    inter = a.intersect(r).Volume()
55|    return (a.Volume() + r.Volume() - 2 * inter) / r.Volume()
56|
57|
58|def score(answer, reference, expected):
59|    """PASS if every check holds. Returns (passed, failed_checks, measurements)."""
60|    m = measure(answer)
61|    fails = compare(m, expected)
62|    try:
63|        d = mismatch(answer, reference)
64|    except Exception as e:  # a broken shape can't be intersected
65|        d, fails = None, fails + [f"mismatch error {e!r}"[:120]]
66|    m["mismatch"] = None if d is None else round(d, 5)
67|    if d is not None and d > TOL_DIFF:
68|        fails.append(f"mismatch {d:.1%}")
69|    return (not fails), fails, m

Every job text fixes all positions from the origin (millimetres, Z up), so a correct answer has exactly one shape.
A builder takes keyword overrides; the reference uses the defaults and each wrong version changes one thing.
"""
import math

import cadquery as cq
from cadquery import Solid, Vector


def box(x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1):
    return Solid.makeBox(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, z1 - z0, Vector(x0, y0, z0))


def cyl(r, p, d, h):
    """Cylinder of radius r starting at point p, going h along direction d."""
    return Solid.makeCylinder(r, h, Vector(*p), Vector(*d))


def zcyl(r, x, y, z0, z1):
    return cyl(r, (x, y, z0), (0, 0, 1), z1 - z0)


def slot_z(cx, cy, length, width, z0, z1):
    """Obround slot along X: straight part (length - width) plus two round ends, total length `length`."""
    half = (length - width) / 2
    s = box(cx - half, cx + half, cy - width / 2, cy + width / 2, z0, z1)
    s = s.fuse(zcyl(width / 2, cx - half, cy, z0, z1)).fuse(zcyl(width / 2, cx + half, cy, z0, z1))
    return s


def prism_xy(points, z0, z1):
    return cq.Workplane("XY").polyline(points).close().extrude(z1 - z0).translate((0, 0, z0)).val()


def _prism_yz(points, x0, x1):
    # Build in XY with (u, v) = (y, z), extrude along +Z by (x1 - x0), then map (u, v, t) -> (t, u, v).
    w = cq.Workplane("XY").polyline(points).close().extrude(x1 - x0).val()
    m = cq.Matrix([[0, 0, 1, x0], [1, 0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0, 0]])

+

+def tag_failure(finish_reason, content, run_error, built, fails):
+    """One of api_error / wrong_geometry / INVALID (PLAN failure tags).
+
+    api_error: the answer raised during the run (AttributeError,
+    TypeError, NameError, Part errors, timeout, memory limit,
+    PermissionError, refused import, no network in the box).
+    wrong_geometry: it built but failed the checker, or `result` was not
+    a Part solid. A reply cut off by the token limit is INVALID.
+    """
+    if finish_reason == "length":
+        return "INVALID"
+    if not content or not content.strip():
+        return "INVALID"
+    err = run_error or ""
+    if "not a Part solid" in err or "no variable named 'result'" in err:
+        return "wrong_geometry"
+    if built and fails:
+        return "wrong_geometry"
+    if built and not fails:
+        return ""
+    if err:
+        return "api_error"
+    return "wrong_geometry"
+
+
+def outcome_of(finish_reason, content, call_error):
+    """INVALID for cut-offs, empty replies, and failed calls after the
+    retry (as in the baseline); else None (the box + grader decide)."""
+    if call_error is not None:
+        return "INVALID"
+    if finish_reason == "length":
+        return "INVALID"
+    if not content or not content.strip():
+        return "INVALID"
+    return None
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------- Wonder money
+
+
+def cost_w_of_usage(usage):
+    """Wonder $: reasoning tokens are billed as output (same completion
+    count); cached input at $0.20/M."""
+    usage = usage or {}
+    try:
+        prompt = float(usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0) or 0)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        prompt = 0.0
+    try:
+        completion = float(usage.get("completion_tokens", 0) or 0)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        completion = 0.0
+    try:
+        cached = float(usage.get("cached_tokens", 0) or 0)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        cached = 0.0
+    return (prompt * COST_W_IN_PER_M + completion * COST_W_OUT_PER_M
+            + cached * COST_W_CACHED_PER_M) / 1e6
+
+
+def cost_w_total(w_usages):
+    return sum(cost_w_of_usage(u) for u in w_usages)
+
+
+def over_budget_w(w_usages, budget_w):
+    return cost_w_total(w_usages) > budget_w
+
+
+def cached_tokens_of(usage):
+    try:
+        return int((usage or {}).get("cached_tokens", 0) or 0)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        return 0

Part A — new files in [experiments/freecad](~/projects/forge/experiments/freecad):
- [run_one_fc.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/freecad/run_one_fc.py): box-side answer runner (exec with `__main__`, Part-solid check, cadquery/OCP hook, writes answer.step + measure.json).
- [cloud_exec.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/freecad/cloud_exec.py): box config (block_network, cpu 1, 1–4 GiB, 90 s; exec timeout 60; 20 MB STEP cap; image files `["run_one_fc.py"]`) and the write/run/read-back/terminate flow.
- [cloud_grade.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/freecad/cloud_grade.py): grader (verdict at 0.2%, recording at 1e-6; loads expected.json only in the image build/grader, never prints it).
- [runner_fc.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/freecad/runner_fc.py): imports request/retry/extract/budget/k-workers helpers from frozen `runner.py`; FreeCAD prompt, manual hash refusal, arms G/S/W with escalation, api_error/wrong_geometry/INVALID tags, T = S ∪ W-rescues, PLAN rules 1–5 on T and S, calls.jsonl/summary.json/report.md, full CLI including `--escalate-from`, `--budget-w`, `--w-smoke`, `--w-endpoint`.
- [run_fc_session.sh](~/projects/forge/experiments/freecad/run_fc_session.sh): wrapper setting the existing `RUN_SESSION_RUNNER_CMD` hook (run_session.sh untouched).
- [test_fc_cloud.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/freecad/test_fc_cloud.py), [test_runner_fc.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/freecad/test_runner_fc.py): 34 offline tests (fake sandboxes/HTTP/Part; every Modal-reaching path monkeypatched to raise).

Part B — changed [forge_train.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/train/forge_train.py) (Round 2 only): remote calls wrapped in `modal.enable_output()` + `app.run()`; `STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S` 600→300; guard raises when references unbuildable; serve ready wait 8 min→`SERVE_READY_S` with request timeout 120 s; never-`modal-run` docstring. Plus 5 tests in [test_forge_train.py](~/projects/forge/experiments/train/test_forge_train.py) and exactly one added line in [README.md](~/projects/forge/README.md). Verified live: `smoke --cap-dollars 2.0` prints CAP REFUSED, exit 2.

Two deviations to know about. The import hook alone cannot refuse `cadquery` when it is already imported, so `run_answer_source` also masks refused modules from `sys.modules` during exec (no-op in the real box, where it is not installed). And `runner_fc.py` builds FreeCAD messages as system + manual message + job message (the arm-B layout) rather than one combined user message, since the spec cites both wordings.
